circuits_array.note: every circuit is one direct crossing (OWNER 10-21: board trace / DAC / AEC, no switch); per die 5 = 3 TP endpoints (6 TP circuits x 2 ends / 4 dies) + stage NEXT + stage PREV

reuse: per the token DAG of record (results/arch/token_path_20261009/ds_rom.json) every layer writes and reads its own rows on its own stage (own_row_write / window_load / pv nodes); what later layers reuse from the owner layers 2/8/14/20 is the top-k selection, which rides the stage h message with the user tag. So copy B needs NO reuse link; the owner copy is addressed by user only through the h message order. Lane MU-S81/SVC confirms on the RTL (svc_bases.json).

stage_hop.circuit: s_0N pair A (TX, every window ab 0) -> next stage rank r s_0N pair B (RX -> ri)
stage_hop.windows: 4 back-to-back 80-beat tag windows (NB 80, 4 mu_c a hop; lead 10-21)
stage_hop.E_basis: record token_compose stage_hop: 538 measured + off-chip leg (OWNER 10-21 direct cabling: stage_hop D_cycles_max 265, results/arch/release_rack_1021/hop_latency.json @5a1c6dcea systems.S81.<class>.D_cycles_max; was 453 switched) + 134 priced on-die legs (results/rtl/xdie_s81_1019/record.json)
stage_hop.was: folded onto the ES TP circuit (tb_xdie_s81 d -> d+1 inside the group): no real circuit to the next stage existed on the 4-endpoint die
stage_hop.per_token_delta_why: LINK5 itself: 0 (the composition of record already prices every hop as ONE crossing of 321 beats on one port; LINK5 makes that crossing real). Direct cabling: every crossing's 453 switched leg -> its class D (see calendar_<mode>.json offchip.saving). MU calendar: the fold had 0 collisions at stage granularity (min AR margin slot - (span + h) = 690.7 cycles, S005), the LINK5 calendar has 0 collisions with the s_0N TX / RX resources

latency.copy_a: unchanged (the latency user is always on copy A: same dies, same circuits)
latency.why: direct cabling (OWNER 10-21): copy-B circuits copyb_in 258 / copyb_out 257 / copyb_hop 265 <= stage_hop 265 cycles, so copy B's hop is never later than copy A's; a copy-B user's windows are the copy-A windows shifted by its slot
